belief: Because church people hurt me, God must be just like them.
origins: When those who speak for God use that voice to control, shame, or harm, it is hard to separate them from God. A pastor’s betrayal, a youth leader’s abuse of trust, or a church’s harsh rejection can leave a child or adult convinced that God shares their coldness or cruelty.
teaches: Scripture describes God’s own character: “The LORD, the LORD God, is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion and faithfulness.” “The LORD is near to the brokenhearted; He saves the contrite in spirit.” Of His servant it says, “A bruised reed He will not break and a smoldering wick He will not extinguish.” The writer of Hebrews says that Jesus, our high priest, sympathizes with our weaknesses. God never promised that every person speaking in His name reflects Him. The measure of God is Jesus, who was gentle with the wounded and angry only at those who burdened them.
self_statements: If that is what Christians are like, I want nothing to do with God.
God let them do it, so He must be like them.
They spoke for God, so God must agree with them.
I cannot trust God after that.
God is as harsh as they were.
errors: Letting a few people stand for God and all believers.
Feeling betrayed and concluding God is the same.
Believing the church and God are either both good or both bad.
Judging God by those who claimed to represent Him.
questions: What exactly was done to me, and who did it?
Did those people actually reflect God’s character as Scripture describes it?
How does Jesus treat people who are hurt by religious leaders?
Is it fair to judge God by those who misrepresented Him?
What do I want God to be like?
What would it look like to read the Gospels to see Jesus for myself?
truth: People who hurt me in God’s name misrepresented Him. God is compassionate, gracious, and near to the brokenhearted. I can grieve what was done and take my time getting to know the real God through Jesus.
hw_truths: He is near to the brokenhearted.
He does not break a bruised reed.
Those who hurt me did not speak for Him.
I can come to God at my own pace.
log: Each week, write one trait of God from Scripture that differs from how I was treated.
actions: Write the facts of what was done in God’s name.
Tell a counselor or trusted friend; seek legal and safe help if abuse occurred.
Read Mark slowly and note how Jesus treated hurting people.
Tell God your anger and hurt.
prayer: Lord, I was hurt by people who spoke in Your name. Show me who You really are. Heal my wounds and help me meet You through Jesus, gentle with the broken. Amen.
hw_questions: What was done in God’s name?
How is God different from them?
How does Jesus treat the hurt?
Who can I get support from?
What do I need from God?
What can I read about Jesus?
name_example: Sarah can write: “The Lord is compassionate and gracious, unlike those who hurt me.”
